headline: Source-aligned agent-memory units improve complete-evidence retrieval in a synthetic trace benchmark
summary: A paper introduces Execution Provenance Graph Memory (EPGM) for retrieving complete supporting evidence from long agent execution histories under a fixed token budget. On 2,000 queries over 1,207 held-out ISETrace trajectories, the authors report that source-aligned provenance units improve Full Support@2048 by 19.07 points over flat 512-token windows and by 11.96 points over a per-metric oracle across four flat chunk sizes, with matched Dense-FT scoring. Holding candidate units and seed scores fixed, a graph-conditioned residual adds a smaller 4.55 points (95% CI 2.98–6.18), concentrated on queries whose evidence spans multiple events. The corpus is synthetic and the results are author-reported; no independent reproduction was performed.
